chunks: Abu Nasr Hibatullah said: Abu Ahmad Daranawayh the Leper, whose house was in the Alley of the Stationers, narrated to me, saying: I and my brothers used to enter to Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, may Allah be pleased with him, to transact business with him.

He was a merchant and we were about ten people; nine of us would curse him and one would be unsure. So we would leave him after entering to him: nine of us would seek proximity to Allah through his love, and one would remain standing (unsure), because he would accompany us with the excellence of the Companions, what we had narrated and what we had not narrated, so we would write it down for his goodness from him, may Allah be pleased with him.

key_terms.أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ رُوعٍ: Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh (a prominent Shia leader)
key_terms.دَرْبُ الْقَرَّاطِيسِ: Alley of the Stationers (a location in Baghdad)

ai.seo_question: What was the nature of the scholarly interaction between the companions and Husayn ibn Ruh regarding the virtues of the Companions?
ai.summary: This narrative from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the intellectual rigor of the Four Deputies' era, where the presence of Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh (the second major deputy) served as a spiritual and scholarly anchor. It highlights the dynamic between the 'nine who curse' (for certainty) and the 'one who doubts' (for humility), demonstrating how the Companions' virtues were preserved and authenticated through direct interaction with the Imam's representative.
